intro: You are standing at Domuztepe, a mound in Kahramanmaraş province, around 6000 BC. This was the largest known settlement of the Halaf culture. It also holds a mass burial called the Death Pit — one of the most argued-over finds in prehistoric Anatolia.
history: This mound on the Kahramanmaraş plain is the largest known settlement of the Halaf culture, dating to the sixth millennium BC. Excavations from the 1990s uncovered the mass burial known as the Death Pit. Inside it, the disarticulated bones of at least thirty-five people were found mixed with animal bone. What happened here? What the deposit means is still argued over.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Death Pit, the Halaf painted pottery, the round buildings and the seal impressions.
facts: Did you know? Five explanations have been proposed for the Death Pit: warfare, epidemic, ritual feasting, ancestor rites and cannibalism. Yet none of them accounts for everything found in it. The mound is the largest known settlement of the Halaf culture and dates to the sixth millennium BC. In the Death Pit, the disarticulated bones of at least thirty-five people lay mixed with animal bone, and what it means is still argued over today.
outro: This brings our tour of Domuztepe to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This mound still guards its questions; let it keep them for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
